newsitem.title: USA: GM says has tentative pact at Ohio plant.
newsitem.headline: GM says has tentative pact at Ohio plant.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Monday it has reached tentative agreement with a union representing 4,100 workers at its Moraine, Ohio, sport utility vehicle assembly plant and has averted a possible strike.

"We have a tentative agreement," reached late last week, GM spokesman Tom Beaman of GM's truck group headquarters in Pontiac, Mich., said in a telephone interview. "The ratification will proceed as soon as possible, and there is not going to be any disruption."
Local 801 of the International Union of Electronic Workers had notified GM early last week it would strike at 0001 EST/0501 GMT Tuesday if progress was not made on a new three-year pact.

Earlier Monday a union official told Reuters the strike notice had been withdrawn although there was still some language to work out. Local president Willie Thorpe said he felt the sides could work things out.
The plant, near Dayton, assembles Chevrolet Blazer, GMC Jimmy and Oldsmobile Bravada sport utility vehicles.
